title: Name every plan-declared produce/consume artifact in the Bun code that moves it through Cargo

facts.note: Necessary but not sufficient: TS/JS alone does not distinguish Bun from Node.js or Deno.
Bun stack identity needs a repo-level observer (e.g. the consumer's configured stack / Bun runtime markers); the rule is Bun-only.
Wagon documents live under plan/**; their produce[].name / consume[].name entries define the contract.
A wagon implementation is recognised structurally (a module that moves artifacts through Cargo, e.g. cargo.get/cargo.put), not by filename; needs a structural observer.

Whether any wagon implementation exists (Cargo-moving code present) vs. contract declared with no implementation at all; needed to apply the NOT_APPLICABLE case. Wagon-to-module association is not explicit in the source detector, which checks names against Cargo-moving modules.
Emitted by the bun_interlocking_infrastructure family detector (checks/wagon_contract_honoured.mjs).
Diff-level facts: contract entries edited or Cargo-moving code changed.

fires: In a Bun repository, a wagon document under plan/** declares a produce[] or consume[] artifact name that no Cargo-moving Bun module names, while an implementation of that wagon exists.
A Cargo-moving Bun module is edited and stops naming an artifact its wagon document still declares.
A wagon document gains a new produce[]/consume[] entry while a wagon implementation already exists, and no Cargo-moving Bun module names the newly declared artifact.
doesNotFire: The consumer repository declares no wagon contract at all.
A wagon is declared in the plan but has no implementation anywhere (unimplemented feature, governed by another rule).
A contract entry is added and the Cargo-moving code already names (or is updated to name) that artifact.
Non-Bun stacks (including Node.js or Deno TypeScript/JavaScript).
Only the shape of the wagon document is wrong (core wagon.schema.json validation, not this rule).

given: A wagon document under plan/** declares its data contract — produce[]: artifacts the wagon owns; consume[]: artifacts it takes from other wagons — and Bun code moves Cargo for that wagon
when: the wagon's Cargo-moving code or its declared contract is written or changed
then: Name every declared produce[].name and consume[].name artifact in the Bun module(s) where that wagon moves Cargo, so declaration and carried data cannot drift apart.
prefer: Plan-matching name constants used at the Cargo call sites: `export const CONSUMES = "orders:priced-basket"; // plan: consume[].name` / `export const PRODUCES = "orders:confirmed-order"; // plan: produce[].name`; in `runWagon(step, cargo)`: `const basket = cargo.get(CONSUMES); cargo.put(PRODUCES, { confirmed: true, basket });`.
If the wagon no longer owns an artifact, correct the plan instead.
Name your modules as you like; no particular filename is required — what matters is that the module moving the wagon's Cargo names its artifacts.
avoid: Plan produce/consume lists diverging from what is actually put/got through Cargo.
Putting a wagon's declared names only in a shared or unrelated module that does not move that wagon's Cargo.
Trying to suppress a finding: it is not suppressible.
unless: The consumer declares no wagon contract (NOT_APPLICABLE).
The wagon has no implementation anywhere: an unimplemented feature, not a broken contract; another rule governs it.
why: Core wagon.schema.json only checks the contract is well formed; only a detector reading Bun source and its Cargo idiom can see whether the code carries the declared artifacts.
evidence: For every wagon document under plan/** with an implementation, each produce[].name and consume[].name string appears in at least one Cargo-moving Bun module.
checks/wagon_contract_honoured.mjs reports no findings; CI passes (strict, not suppressible).
verifier_detail: Read every wagon document under plan/**; collect produce[].name and consume[].name artifact names; flag any name that no Cargo-moving module names.

Core wagon.schema.json requires both produce (artifacts the wagon owns) and consume (artifacts it takes from other wagons), each entry carrying an artifact `name` (and, for produce, a `contract` and `telemetry` URN); core validates that shape wherever the plan lives, but cannot know whether a Bun module puts those artifacts into Cargo, because that means reading Bun source and this stack's Cargo idiom.

Recognise the wagon implementation STRUCTURALLY — a module that moves artifacts through Cargo — never by filename. A `wagon.ts` naming heuristic is the kind of fitted check this hub has had to unpick more than once; consumers may name modules as they like.

NOT_APPLICABLE, deliberately, in two cases: (1) consumer declares no wagon contract — nothing to honour; (2) contract declared with no wagon implementation at all — an unimplemented feature, not a broken contract, belonging to whatever rule governs unimplemented plan; reporting it here would fire on every freshly planned repository. The rule judges code that exists against the contract it claims, not the absence of code.

Member of the bun_interlocking_infrastructure FAMILY detector (checks/wagon_contract_honoured.mjs). Severity 4, disposition strict: a wagon whose declared contract nothing implements is not suppressible and fails CI.
Term wagon_data_contract: the artifacts a wagon document declares under produce[] and consume[], each identified by an artifact `name`, which the wagon's Cargo-moving code must name.
